THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE ASHOK S.KINAGI  ORAL ORDER
This writ petition is filed challenging the order on IA.No.1 dated 21.06.2024 passed in MC.No.5/2023 by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Arakalagudu.
The brief facts giving rise to the filing of this writ petition are as under:
The petitioner filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
In the said proceedings the respondent filed a IA.No.1. under Section 24 of Hindu Marriage Act seeking interim maintenance of Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioner opposed the said application.
The trial Court after hearing the parties allowed the application in part.

The petitioner was directed to pay Rs.5,000/- per month towards the interim maintenance from the date of filing I.A. till the disposal of the petition and the petitioner was directed to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards litigation expenses.
The petitioner aggrieved by the order on IA.No.1 filed this Writ petition.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is getting a salary of Rs.23,912/-.
Hence, he submits that the interim maintenance awarded by the trial NC: 2024:KHC:50867 Court is exorbitant.
On these grounds, he prays to allow the Writ petition.
4. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner.
There is no dispute regarding the relationship between the petitioner and respondent.
The relationship between the petitioner and respondent is not cordial.
Both are residing separately.

sentences.text: Further the respondent had no source of income for maintaining herself.
The respondent filed an application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
The petitioner is working in BMTC and drawing salary of more than Rs.25,000/-.

The trial Court considering the monthly income of the petitioner has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/-
towards monthly interim maintenance.
The interim maintenance awarded by the trial Court is just and proper.
I do not find any error in the impugned order.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The Writ petition is dismissed.
